reasoning: Identity confirmed: EO 10955, July 31, 1961, 26 FR 6967, administration of assistance for Latin American development and the reconstruction of Chile. Inventory complete: sec. 1 (delegation of the functions under secs. 2 and 3 of the Act of September 8, 1960) and sec. 2 (allocation of funds); the order has no other operative text and no own-terms end. EO 10973 sec. 605(c) supersedes 'Executive Order No. 10955 of July 31, 1961 (26 F.R. 6967)' without exception, and sec. 607 makes 'The provisions of this order' effective 'as of September 30, 1961'. That clause covers the supersession provision itself, so the end date for both clauses and the whole order is 1961-09-30, not the signing date of 1961-11-03. The actor is EO 10973 (President Kennedy) and the mechanism is express supersession. No earlier end exists: the cruden search and the dossier chain show EO 10973 as the only acting instrument. Sec. 101 re-delegates to the Secretary of State the functions under the Latin America act, as the claim says. The sec. 606 savings is paraphrased accurately, and the transferred_or_accrued state is supported. The structured dates now agree with the judgment reasons and the research rationale, and the order-level end equals the latest clause end. The searches are described honestly.
